title: Italian Game
author: LlamaChess Repertoire
description: The Italian Game (1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4) — 22 interactive lines with c3, d4 center attacks, and casual notes.

steps.title: Rook Gambit — Greco Punish
steps.theory: Let's learn the Italian game! This is by far the most played opening at the non-professional level. It's traditional, it's old school, it's chess the way your grandpa taught you. Let's just get into it with pawn to e4.

steps.title: 1.e4
steps.theory: Let's get started with pawn to e4.

steps.title: e5
steps.theory: Black responds ...e5 — the classical fight for the center.

steps.title: 2.Nf3
steps.theory: Knight to f3, attacking Black's e5 pawn. You've probably done this a million times.

steps.title: 3.Bc4
steps.theory: Bishop to c4 — this targets f7, the weakest pawn in Black's position. Mamma mia!

steps.title: Bc5
steps.theory: The Giuoco Piano: Black mirrors with ...Bc5.

steps.title: 4.c3
steps.theory: The Italian move — pawn to c3, setting up d4 to attack that bishop.

steps.title: 5.d4
steps.theory: Now the center break: pawn to d4!

steps.title: 6.cxd4
steps.theory: Recapture with cxd4 — keep pressure on the bishop.

steps.title: 7.Nc3
steps.theory: Develop with Nc3 — protect the king and offer the e4 pawn.

steps.title: 8.O-O
steps.theory: Ignore the threats — just castle! Development beats everything.

steps.title: Nxc3
steps.theory: Black takes on c3 with the knight.

steps.title: 10.Ba3
steps.theory: Sacrifice the rook! Bishop to a3 — Black cannot castle anymore.

steps.title: Bxa1
steps.theory: Black took the bait with ...Bxa1. They lost the game!

steps.title: 11.Re1+
steps.theory: Rook to e1+, checking the king.

steps.title: 12.Bxe7
steps.theory: Grab the knight — bishop takes e7.

steps.title: 13.Rxe7+
steps.theory: Rook takes e7+, winning the queen.

steps.title: 14.Qxa1
steps.theory: Finally queen to a1 — you're up a whole knight. Wow!

steps.title: Pinning Pressure — vs ...d6
steps.theory: Smart opponents block your Ba3 with ...d6 instead of grabbing the rook. No problem — slide the rook to c1 and pin them to death.

steps.title: d6
steps.theory: Ah — Black blocks with ...d6 so they can still castle.

steps.title: 11.Rc1
steps.theory: Slide the rook to c1 — hit the bishop and gain a tempo.

steps.title: 12.Qa4
steps.theory: Awesome move: queen to a4 — pins the knight to the king!

steps.title: 13.d5
steps.theory: Pawn to d5 — the knight is the only defender of the bishop.

steps.title: 14.Nxe5
steps.theory: First knight takes knight on e5.

steps.title: 15.Qxa5
steps.theory: Now queen takes a5 — free bishop! Up a piece and ahead in development.

steps.title: Queen Skewer — vs ...Bb4
steps.theory: When Black tries ...Bb4 instead of taking the rook, trade bishops and unleash a queen skewer on the king and knight.

steps.title: 12.Qe1+
steps.theory: Queen to e1+ — hitting the king AND the knight. Can you spot the fork?

steps.title: 13.Qxb4
steps.theory: Snap off the free knight — queen takes b4. Up a piece, castled, winning.

steps.title: Pawn Phalanx — vs ...Bb6
steps.theory: When Black retreats the bishop to b6 instead of checking, march your pawns forward and humiliate their knights.

steps.title: Bb6
steps.theory: Retreating to b6 was a huge mistake.

steps.title: Nh6
steps.theory: Knight retreats to h6 — gross, on the rim.

steps.title: 9.d5
steps.theory: Now pawn to d5 — harass the other knight in the center.

steps.title: 10.Bg5
steps.theory: Bishop to g5, attacking the queen-side.

steps.title: 11.exf6
steps.theory: Sacrifice with exf6 — you're threatening fxg7 with discovered attack. +4 on the eval bar!

steps.title: Queen's Assault — Two Knights
steps.theory: Against the Two Knights Defense, strike with d4 immediately. When Black grabs on e4, queen to d5 wins it back with interest.

steps.title: 5.dxe5
steps.theory: Recapture on e5 — open the d-file for your queen.

steps.title: 6.Qd5
steps.theory: Better than defending f2 — queen to d5, hitting e4 AND f7!

steps.title: Bxf2+
steps.theory: Bishop check on f2 — that's fine.

steps.title: 7.Kf1
steps.theory: King to f1. All part of the plan.

steps.title: 8.Qxe4
steps.theory: Queen takes e4 — simply up a piece. Well done!

steps.title: Two Knights Fork — Re1 & Nc3
steps.theory: The textbook Two Knights punishment: castle, pin with Re1, and fork queen and knight with Nc3.

steps.title: 5.O-O
steps.theory: Castle first — get the king safe.

steps.title: 6.Re1
steps.theory: Rook to e1 — pin the knight to the king!

steps.title: 8.Nc3
steps.theory: Nc3 — fork! Queen and pinned knight. White wins the piece back with the better game.

steps.title: Møller Attack — 9.d5
steps.theory: Instead of recapturing on c3, push d5! The Møller Attack wins back the piece with a raging initiative on the open e-file.

steps.title: Bxc3
steps.theory: Black takes on c3 with the bishop.

steps.title: 9.d5
steps.theory: Don't recapture — push d5! Hit the knight and open lines.

steps.title: 10.Re1
steps.theory: Rook to e1 — the e-file is a highway to Black's king.

steps.title: 11.Rxe4
steps.theory: Rook takes e4 — piece back, huge attack coming. Bg5 and Nd5 ideas next.

steps.title: Philidor Sideline — 2...d6
steps.theory: When Black ducks with ...d6, open the center anyway and build a kingside attack while they sit cramped.

steps.title: O-O
steps.theory: Qd2 — connect rooks and prepare long castle. Space advantage locked in.

steps.title: Giuoco Pianissimo — Quiet d3
steps.theory: Not every Italian has to be a gambit. Sometimes d3, castle, and Re1 is all you need against a passive opponent.

steps.title: 7.Re1
steps.theory: Rook to e1 — pressure on e5 builds. Classic Italian principles.

steps.title: Steady Giuoco — 7...d6
steps.theory: When Black plays ...d6 instead of taking on e4, push d5 and finish development with a space edge.

steps.title: O-O
steps.theory: Black castles. You're slightly better with more room to operate.

steps.title: Greco Gambit — Declined Sac
steps.theory: When Black takes on e4 but avoids ...Nxc3, keep developing — your lead in pieces wins the day.

steps.title: 10.Be3
steps.theory: Be3 — solid central bishop, finish development. Initiative stays with White.

steps.title: Two Knights — 5.e5
steps.theory: When Black avoids the pawn grab with ...exd4, push e5 and drive the knight back with gain of time.

steps.title: exd4
steps.theory: exd4 — Black declines the gambit line.

steps.title: 6.Bd5
steps.theory: Bishop to d5 — strong central bishop, attacking c6. White stands better.

steps.title: Hungarian Defense — 3...Be7
steps.theory: Black plays the Hungarian ...Be7 instead of ...Bc5. Develop simply and open the center when ready.

steps.title: 7.O-O
steps.theory: You castle too — slight edge with the better bishop pair potential.

steps.title: Center Blast — 4.d4 vs ...Bc5
steps.theory: Skip c3 and hit d4 one move earlier? Sometimes — but c3 first is safer. Here's the full c3-d4 plan when Black stays on c5.

steps.title: 7.Be3
steps.theory: Bishop to e3 — solid central bishop, eyeing the queenside. Good practical chances.

steps.title: vs ...a6
steps.theory: Black plays ...a6 to stop Nb5 tricks. Keep developing — the Italian doesn't need tricks to be good.

steps.title: 7.Re1
steps.theory: Re1 — standard Italian pressure on e5.

steps.title: Two Knights — Early ...d5
steps.theory: If Black tries ...d5 too early in the Two Knights, exploit the loose central pawns.

steps.title: 6.Qe2
steps.theory: Qe2 — pin the knight to the king. White keeps a strong initiative.

steps.title: Philidor — ...Nbd7
steps.theory: A common Philidor tabiya. Develop naturally and prepare f4 or c4 breaks.

steps.title: 6.O-O
steps.theory: Black castles. Equal but you have easier plans.

steps.title: vs ...Qe7
steps.theory: Black develops the queen early — often a sign they're unsure. Develop fast and open the center.

steps.title: Be6
steps.theory: Black develops ...Be6. You have easier piece play and more space.

steps.title: Giuoco — ...d5 break
steps.theory: When Black tries ...d5 in the Giuoco, capture and keep pieces active.

steps.title: Bb4+
steps.theory: Bb4+ — sharp but fine for White with Nc3 next.

steps.title: Two Knights — Decline ...Bxf2+
steps.theory: If you're ahead in development after ...Bxf2+, sometimes Ke2 is enough — but Kf1 and Qxe4 is cleaner.

steps.title: 6.Bb5+
steps.theory: Bb5+ — fork tricks on c6/d7. Sharp and fun.

steps.title: Quiet Italian — 4.d3 vs ...Nf6
steps.theory: Prefer a quieter fight? d3 against ...Nf6 avoids the wildest gambits but keeps a small edge.

steps.title: 6.Re1
steps.theory: Re1 — classic Italian development. Solid and strong.

steps.title: Main Line Finish — Re8 pressure
steps.theory: The bread-and-butter Italian: develop, castle, rook e1, and push d4 when the time is right.

steps.title: 8.Nbd2
steps.theory: Nbd2 — finish development. You're ready for d4 or f4 later. Spicy meatball complete!
